question: The function $f(x)$ is defined as $f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{|x|},&|x|\ge2\\a+bx^2,&|x|\le2\end{cases}$, where $a$ and $b$ are known constants. Then, only one of the following statements is true. Which one is it?

options.A: $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=-2$ if and only if $a=\frac34$ and $b=-\frac1{16}$
options.B: $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=-2$, whatever be the values of $a$ and $b$
options.C: $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=-2$, if $b=-\frac1{16}$, whatever be the value of $a$
options.D: $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=-2$, if $b=\frac1{16}$, whatever be the value of $a$

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level
